name: value_accounts
title: Value Accounts
description: A place where value sits. A business does not hold only 'cash in the bank' -- it holds a checking account, maybe bitcoin or a stablecoin, a box of physical cash in the till, a credit line, gift cards, possibly a weight of metal -- and those differ along axes the chart of accounts alone never records: what unit they are denominated in, WHO HOLDS THEM, who may move them, and how you would ever prove the balance is real. This collection is the generalization of bank_accounts (which it supersedes -- a box of cash is not a bank account, and calling it one is the kind of naming debt that confuses a system for years). Each row still points at exactly one book account through fin_account_id: reconciliation compares two independent truths and never merges them. The verification field is the important one -- it says what class of evidence exists for this account, and by extension how much a reconciliation of it is worth (see plan/value-accounts-and-denominations-spec.md). A blockchain balance is stronger evidence than a bank statement, because anyone can verify it and no institution has to be trusted. A physical count is the weakest, because it is self-certification: the person counting the till is usually the person who could take from it, which is why requires_second_attestor exists and why cash businesses have always used two-person counts. Recording that difference honestly, rather than presenting every reconciliation as equally trustworthy, is the point.

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.help: How you refer to it: 'Business Checking', 'Front Register', 'Cold Wallet'.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind
fields.help: What sort of place this is. Drives which verification is even possible and how much assurance it carries.

fields.name: denomination_id
fields.label: Denomination
fields.help: The unit this account holds (USD, BTC, XAU, a gift-card program). Amounts are integers of this denomination's smallest unit -- see object_money.py.

fields.name: fin_account_id
fields.label: Book Account
fields.help: The account in the chart of accounts whose balance this place must agree with. Without it, nothing can be reconciled or posted.

fields.name: custody
fields.label: Custody
fields.help: Who physically or cryptographically holds the value. institution: a bank or exchange holds it and can restore your access. self: you hold it -- a till, a hardware wallet, a safe; nobody can restore it for you. third_party: someone else holds it on your behalf.

fields.name: custodian
fields.label: Custodian
fields.help: Named holder: 'Chase', 'Coinbase', 'Ledger in the office safe', 'front register'.

fields.name: reference
fields.label: Reference
fields.help: Last four digits, a blockchain address, a card reference. Never a full account number.

fields.name: verification
fields.label: Verification
fields.help: How the balance is proven. statement_import: the institution sends a statement. chain_query: read the address on a public ledger -- the strongest evidence there is, verifiable by anyone. physical_count: someone counts it, which is self-certification unless witnessed. issuer_balance: the issuer states a number with no line-item history. none: unverified, and the reconciliation view says so.

fields.name: managed_by
fields.label: Managed By
fields.help: Who is responsible for this account day to day -- deliberately separate from owner_id, because the person who reconciles the register should not have to be the person who can move the wire. Separation of duties as a field rather than a policy document.

fields.name: requires_second_attestor
fields.label: Requires Witness
fields.help: For self-certified verification (a cash count): whether a second person must attest before the count is accepted. The classic control against the person who counts being the person who could take.

fields.name: last_proven_control_at
fields.label: Control Last Proven
fields.help: Self-custody only, and the field no other asset class needs: a chain balance proves the funds exist at an address, NOT that you still hold the key. A bank can restore access; a lost seed phrase is permanent. This records the last time control was actually demonstrated (an outbound transaction, a signed message, a restore test).

fields.name: entity_id
fields.label: Entity
fields.help: The set of books this account belongs to (65 multi-entity).
